q-12556.name: Question 1
q-12556.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{x{e}^{-3x}}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x{e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the integral ∫xe−3xdx.

a
e−3x3−xe−3x9+C
b
xe−3x9+e−3x9+C
c
xe−3x9−e−3x3+C
d
−xe−3x3−e−3x9+C
e

Submit

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫xe−3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=e−3x⟹v=−e−3x3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅e−3xdx=x⋅(−e−3x3)−∫(−e−3x3)⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫xe−3xdx=−xe−3x3+13∫e−3xdx=−xe−3x3−e−3x9+C

q-114289.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{3}^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′} & ={3}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\int \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\int \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{3}^{x}}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3})+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Calculate ∫x3xdx.

a
 3xln⁡3(1ln⁡3−x2)+C
b
 3xln⁡3(x−1)+C
c
 3xln⁡3(x−1ln⁡3)+C
d
 3xln⁡3(x−13)+C
e
 3xln⁡3(2x+1ln⁡3)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫x3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=3x⟹v=3xln⁡3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅3xdx=x⋅3xln⁡3−∫3xln⁡3⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫x3xdx=x3xln⁡3−∫3xln⁡3dx=x3xln⁡3−3x(ln⁡3)2+C=3xln⁡3(x−1ln⁡3)+C

q-114297.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

b

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=cos⁡(3x)⟹v=sin⁡(3x)3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅cos⁡(3x)dx=3x⋅(sin⁡(3x)3)−∫(sin⁡(3x)3)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx=xsin⁡(3x)−∫sin⁡(3x)dx=xsin⁡(3x)+cos⁡(3x)3+C

q-14437.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫2xsin⁡(x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x⟹u′=2v′=sin⁡(x)⟹v=−cos⁡(x).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫2x⋅sin⁡(x)dx=2x⋅(−cos⁡(x))−∫(−cos⁡(x))⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫2xsin⁡(x)dx=−2xcos⁡(x)+2∫cos⁡(x)dx=−2xcos⁡(x)+2sin⁡(x)+C

q-349299.name: Question 5
q-349299.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+4(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 1-0\cdot 0)+4(0-1) \\  & =2\pi -4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-49664.name: Question 6
q-49664.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)]+[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}-0]+[0-1] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
